evidence.claim: polymer_rules.json:classes.PSTR.ff_note: PCFF (Class II) via EMC. TraPPE-UA was rejected: its united-atom representation ignores the phenyl ring partial charges and pi-dihedral barriers that govern PS's Tg (~373K), and no TraPPE-UA PS Tg validation exists. PCFF explicitly parameterizes aromatic C-H charges and cross-terms; Soldera2006 (COMPASS/OPLS) confirms MD reaches PS Tg ~449-484K raw, WLF-corrected ~373K -- no direct PCFF PS Tg paper exists, so confidence is medium. DENSITY CAVEAT: PCFF underpredicts PS 300K density by -5.85% to -6.32% across three independent runs; PCFF's founding paper documents the same aromatic-ring deficit for benzene/toluene (-6.3%/-6.5%), which COMPASS reduces to -1.1%/-1.2% for the same compounds -- field_override='compass' is EMC-admissible but not build-tested against PS's SMILES. Do not generalize this aromatic-ring finding to non-aromatic classes.

evidence.citation: Srivastava, A. et al. On-the-Fly Machine-Learned Force Fields for High-Fidelity Polymer Glass Transition Simulations. arXiv:2601.17137.
evidence.claim: Tg values for 12 polymers; PE Tg=281±52 K; PDMS Tg ~228 K. Validation data for PHYC and PSIL classes.

evidence.citation: Tang, Z.; Okazaki, S. All-Atomistic Molecular Dynamics Study of the Glass Transition of Amorphous Polymers. Polymer 2022, 254, 125044.
evidence.claim: AA-MD glass-transition/dynamics study of polycarbonate (PC) and PMMA via cooling simulations (Tg, radius of gyration, dihedral transitions, end effects, INM). IMPORTANT: PC uses the Kremer et al. force field and PMMA uses OPLS-AA — NEITHER is PCFF. It validates that AA-MD reproduces PC/PMMA Tg & Rg; it does NOT validate PCFF and does NOT benchmark mass density. Do not cite as a PCFF or density source. The 'PCFF PMMA density within 2%' result is NkepsuMbitou2025 (10.1016/j.commatsci.2025.113861, Fig 4 / §5.1).

evidence.citation: Soldera, A.; Metatla, N. Glass Transition of Polymers: Atomistic Simulation versus Experiments. Phys. Rev. E 2006, 74, 061803.
evidence.claim: COMPASS+AMBER/OPLS MD Tg for PE, PMMA, PMA, PS, PMS; WLF analysis shows linear sim-exp correlation. PS Tg WLF-corrected ~373 K (matches experiment). Closest 'any MD Tg' evidence for PSTR; FF is COMPASS/OPLS, not PCFF.

evidence.citation: Nkepsu Mbitou, R. L.; Bedoui, F. A Review on All-Atom Force Fields Capabilities to Predict Polymer Properties: Case of Poly(methyl methacrylate) and Polyisobutylene Polymer Systems. Comput. Mater. Sci. 2025, 253, 113861.
evidence.claim: Systematic review of Class I (GAFF2, OPLS-AA) and Class II (PCFF, CVFF) all-atom FFs for PMMA (PACR) and PIB/polyisobutylene (PHYC); benchmarks thermomechanical properties against experiment. Class II FFs outperform Class I for thermomechanical predictions; informs PACR and PHYC FF confidence notes.

evidence.citation: Klajmon, M. et al. Glass Transition and Structure of Organic Polymers from All-Atom Molecular Simulations. Ind. Eng. Chem. Res. 2023, 62, 21437–21448.
evidence.claim: All-atom MD benchmark for Tg and density of PLA, PEG, and PVP; quantifies equilibration protocol errors and polydispersity effects. Density identified as the most reliable Tg observable regardless of protocol. Informs PEST (PLA) and POXI (PEG) simulation setup. NOTE: paper covers PLA/PEG/PVP — not PC/PA/PEEK as previously annotated.

entanglement_dp_advisory.detail: entanglement MW Me=16600 g/mol for member 'PS' (Mark 2007 Ch.25) / repeat-unit MW 104.2 g/mol -> DP@Me=159 -- reported for context only, not an acceptance criterion for bulk_modulus: entanglement Me governs shear/viscoelastic properties (plateau modulus, reptation), not the isothermal bulk modulus, which is an EOS/local-packing quantity. Establish chain-length convergence of density/K instead (a small DP sweep confirming both plateau) rather than requiring DP>=DP@Me.

nchain_below_production_minimum.detail: nchain=10 is below the advisory PCFF production minimum 20. Its source ("Bejagam 2020") has no copy in this repo and no verified DOI, so the claim is unchecked; nchain>=10 (Wang 2021, verified) IS met, and Hayashi 2022 (RadonPy) ran nchain=10 across 1,077 polymers. Raising nchain to 20 at a fixed system-mass floor would halve per-chain MW (worse chain-length bias); raising it at fixed DP doubles cost for no criterion this module can state. Reported, not applied -- the L>=2*Rg finite-size gate (a separate, already-mechanized check) is the binding constraint on nchain; supply a nchain is now a pure function of the system-mass floor.
